# M5 Diamond-Bar Review — feature/engine-generalization

**Scope:** Phase A (genre-neutralization, INV-14) + Phase B (universal primitives: attributes/inventory/relationships-factions), branched off `master`.
**Build state verified:** branch is `feature/engine-generalization`; diff stat shows the expected A+B surface; per brief tsc 0, 249 tests green.

## Overall Verdict: SHIP WITH FIXES

M5 is disciplined, high-quality work. Phase A is behavior-preserving by construction — registry delegation plus verbatim prose moved into `crime-justice/`. Phase B is purely additive optional state. **No confirmed finding is a live bug or a behavior change against the crime regression oracle.** All 14 confirmed items are latent hazards, double-standard omissions, dead/leaky abstractions, naming warts, or test gaps. There are **0 critical**.

Two themes deserve attention before this engine carries a real attribute/inventory module:

1. **Thin test surface on net-new conserved state.** The B1/B2/B3 primitives have **zero save/load round-trip coverage**, and the load-bearing A4b dialogue-effect extraction seam is only registry-tested. The crime game's behavior-preservation claim for evidence/accusation prose rests on no automated check.
2. **Three real consistency/abstraction defects** accreted in the engine: a shared-helper side effect leaking through a debug route, an SL-07 load-validation double standard, and a fully dead `world.playerState` abstraction.

I independently re-verified the six highest-impact findings against current source (decay-in-shared-helper, advanceMoodMath path, SL-07 asymmetry, dead playerState, trivial A4b test, CRIME_PROSE scope, sole for...in, save-load test gap) — all hold verbatim.

---

## Single Most Important Fix

**Move the attribute-decay step out of the shared `_computeMoodTick` into the real-tick `_tickMoodSystem` only** — `world.ts:556-559`.

`decayAttribute()` now runs inside `_computeMoodTick`, which is also invoked in a `ticks`-long loop by `advanceMoodMath` (`world.ts:803`) — the debug calibration what-if at `routes.ts:1000`, documented *"Mood math only... Use for calibration, not behavior testing."* It iterates the **live** `this.agents` (no clone), so hitting that endpoint silently ages and expires every agent's attribute modifiers, permanently consuming non-self-correcting conserved state (HP regen, wound debuffs, buffs, needs). Latent for the crime game (no attributes), a real corruption vector for any attribute module. The loneliness step already lives in `_tickMoodSystem` (world.ts:577-586) — same precedent, one-line lift.

---

reviews.title: Attribute decay uses for...in on a plain object (prototype pollution risk)
reviews.issue: `for (const key in agent.state.attributes) decayAttribute(...)` uses for...in which iterates inherited prototype properties. While agent.state.attributes is created as a plain `{}` literal (safe in practice), this is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase which uses `for...of Object.entries/keys` or Map iteration. If any library or polyfill ever modifies Object.prototype, this becomes a real bug.
reviews.suggestedFix: Replace with `for (const key of Object.keys(agent.state.attributes))` or use `Object.values` if the key isn't needed.

verify.title: Attribute decay uses for...in on a plain object (consistency wart, prototype-pollution framing overstated)
verify.reasoning: Verified against current source on feature/engine-generalization. world.ts:558 reads `for (const key in agent.state.attributes) decayAttribute(agent.state.attributes[key], 5);` — exactly as cited. A Grep for `for (const X in ...)` across all of packages/ returns this as the SOLE hit, so the "inconsistent with the rest of the codebase" claim is accurate: world.ts otherwise uses Object.entries/keys/values (5 occurrences) and Map iteration (`for (const [, agent] of this.agents)`). The claim that `attributes` is a plain `{}` literal is correct — it is created via `agent.state.attributes = {}` at world.ts:669/678/689 and assigned from JSON.parse output on load at world.ts:1978; both carry only the standard Object.prototype (no enumerable own props), so the loop is functionally safe today. This is therefore a genuine, correctly-scoped MINOR consistency/naming wart at a real location, and it is NOT on the known/accepted residual list. Caveat: the "prototype pollution risk / real bug" justification is overstated — there is no polyfill or dependency mutating Object.prototype in this Bun runtime, and were one to exist that would be the bug, not this loop; the loop iterates a typed `Record<string, ScalarAttribute>`. It is also purely additive B1 state, unused by the crime game, so there is no behavior change vs the regression oracle and no save/load or per-tick hazard introduced. The suggested fix (`for (const key of Object.keys(...))`) is correct and trivial. Confirmed on the consistency merits; the security framing should be discounted.

reviews.title: world.playerState is dead abstraction — never written or read in production

The finding correctly scopes this as latent for the crime game (INV-14: no attributes there) and a real hazard for any attribute-using module. The leak is real (a debug 'mood math' route now ages economy/combat/needs state) and the suggested fix — hoist the decay loop out of _computeMoodTick into _tickMoodSystem (the real-tick path only) — is correct and minimal; the loneliness step at world.ts:577-586 already establishes the precedent of real-tick-only logic living in _tickMoodSystem rather than the shared helper.

reviews.title: Phase B state (attributes/inventory/factions) loaded with no validation — double standard vs SL-07
reviews.issue: moodModifiers are filtered on load for finite magnitude/remaining (world.ts:1976-1977, the SL-07 invariant). The new attributes/factions/inventory are assigned raw from save JSON with no NaN/Infinity guard on attribute.base or modifier magnitudes and no clamp re-validation. A corrupted or hand-edited save with NaN in an attribute base propagates through attributeEffective (clamp(NaN)=NaN) and the decay loop never repairs it. This is the exact double standard the project disallows for new conserved-state primitives.
reviews.suggestedFix: Apply the SL-07 finite-filter on load: drop attribute modifiers with non-finite magnitude/remaining, coerce/clamp attribute.base into [min,max] (re-run createAttribute clamp), and validate inventory quantities are finite positive integers.

verify.title: Phase B state (attributes/inventory/factions) loaded with no SL-07 finite/clamp validation — double standard vs moodModifiers
verify.reasoning:
Mechanism verified against current source on feature/engine-generalization.

ASYMMETRY (the double standard): world.ts:1973-1977 applies SL-07 load validation to mood state — `agent.state.mood = Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, saved.mood))` (clamp) and `moodModifiers = (saved.moodModifiers ?? []).filter(m => Number.isFinite(m?.magnitude) && Number.isFinite(m?.remaining))` (finite filter), under the explicit comment "Validate numeric ranges on load (SL-07)". The immediately following lines world.ts:1978-1980 assign the new Phase B primitives raw: `if (saved.attributes) agent.state.attributes = saved.attributes; if (saved.factions) agent.state.factions = saved.factions; if (saved.inventory) agent.state.inventory = saved.inventory;` — no finite guard, no clamp re-validation, no positive-integer check.

NaN PROPAGATION CONFIRMED: attributes.ts:40-42 `clamp(n,min,max)=Math.max(min,Math.min(max,n))`; with n=NaN, Math.min(max,NaN)=NaN → Math.max(min,NaN)=NaN. So attributeEffective (attributes.ts:49-53) returns NaN for a NaN base. The decay loop decayAttribute (attributes.ts:56-64) mutates only m.remaining and never touches attr.base, and the per-tick caller world.ts:557-558 (`for (const key in agent.state.attributes) decayAttribute(...)`) likewise never repairs base — so a NaN base persists indefinitely, exactly as the finding states. attributeEffective also feeds CG op 'attr' and the scoring-contributor channel, so NaN leaks into utility/rule evaluation.

The primitive is explicitly the generalized MoodModifier (attributes.ts:1-8 "Generalizes the MoodModifier pattern... clamped"), so the SL-07 reasoning transfers directly and was simply not carried over. World writers clamp on the way in (createAttribute attributes.ts:45; setAttribute world.ts:670; adjustAttributeBase world.ts:681) but addAttributeModifier (world.ts:692) pushes mod with NO finite check — unlike mood's addModifier which guards at world.ts:616 — so even a non-corrupt runtime path can write a non-finite attribute modifier that then survives save/load unfiltered. relationships.ts standing/sentiment/trust and inventory.ts quantity have the same raw-load exposure (RelationshipGraph.fromJSON relationships.ts:125-131 stores rels verbatim; inventory assigned raw).

NOT AN ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: the task's known/accepted list is untyped payload keys, the WS crime:scene contract, and the A7b shop→inventory migration — load-time validation of Phase B state is not among them. CLAUDE.md rule #7 "No Double Standards" and the user's memory rule ("default is VIOLATION") make this a tracked violation, not a non-issue.

TEST GAP CORROBORATES: save-load.test.ts has zero round-trip coverage for attributes/inventory/factions and no corrupted-load (NaN/Infinity) test for any field — the SL-07 filter itself is untested.

Severity nuance (honest adversarial discount): in the current regression-oracle crime game these three fields are unused, so there is NO behavior change vs the crime game and no live bug — a NaN base requires a corrupted/hand-edited save or the unguarded addAttributeModifier path. So "major" overstates live impact; "minor/robustness + test gap" is more accurate. But the finding's core claim — an unvalidated load asymmetry that is the exact double standard the project disallows for a new conserved-state primitive — holds with concrete file:line evidence. Suggested fix (drop non-finite attribute modifiers, re-clamp attr.base into [min,max] via createAttribute, validate inventory quantities as finite positive integers) is correct and proportionate.

reviews.title: Residual crime vocabulary in engine public types after the SceneResidue rename
reviews.issue: The rename pass renamed SceneResidue.victimId->affectedId / perpetratorId->actorId but missed DiscoveryContext.victimId (a public engine interface, event-registry.ts:567), the onAgentDeath(killerId, victimId, ...) callback param name (world.ts:55), and the hardcoded perpetratorName: null payload key (world.ts:1529). So within the same interface the rename pass used the neutral `affected*` prefix for the name but left `victimId` as a crime noun.

(2) world.ts:55 — `onAgentDeath?: (killerId: string, victimId: string, killerName: string, affectedName: string) => void;` confirmed in the WorldCallbacks interface. The param is `victimId` (also `killerId`), again paired with the neutral `affectedName`.

The neutrality regex CRIME_PROSE (line 121) includes `perpetrator` but is applied ONLY to string literals (stringLiterals(), line 136), and the comment at line 120 explicitly states "'guard'/'victim' excluded (appear as universal identifiers, not prose)". The `'perpetratorName'` payload key is an object-key identifier (not a quoted string literal), so the literal scanner cannot catch it; it is also the documented accepted untyped-payload residual per the task brief. reviews.title: for...in used in the per-tick attribute decay loop
reviews.issue: The decay loop uses `for (const key in agent.state.attributes)` — the only for...in in the engine. It is the slower idiom (prototype-chain enumeration) and stylistically inconsistent with the codebase's for...of/index loops. Guarded by an existence check so zero-cost for the crime game, but it is on the per-agent-per-5-game-minute hot path for attribute-using modules.
reviews.suggestedFix: Iterate `for (const attr of Object.values(agent.state.attributes)) decayAttribute(attr, 5)`, or store attributes as a Map for the hot path.

verify.title: for...in used in the per-tick attribute decay loop
verify.reasoning:
Verified every sub-claim against current source on feature/engine-generalization.

1. The loop exists verbatim. world.ts:558 — `for (const key in agent.state.attributes) decayAttribute(agent.state.attributes[key], 5);` inside `_computeMoodTick` step 4 (lines 556-559).

2. It is the ONLY for...in in the engine. Grep for `for (const \w+ in ` across packages/engine/src returned exactly one hit (world.ts:558). The codebase otherwise uses for...of / reverse-index loops — e.g. world.ts:519 (`for (let i = mods.length-1...`), world.ts:533 (`for (const rel of ...)`), world.ts:553 (`for (const m of mods)`), attributes.ts:51 and 57. So the stylistic-inconsistency claim holds.

3. It is on the hot path. `_computeMoodTick` is invoked from `_tickMoodSystem` (world.ts:575), which loops over every agent (world.ts:567 `for (const [, agent] of this.agents)`), and `_tickMoodSystem` runs every 5 game minutes via the master clock guard `if (this._gameMinute % 5 === 0)` (world.ts:388-390). The doc comment at world.ts:502 confirms "Called every 5 game minutes." So "per-agent-per-5-game-minute hot path" is accurate.

4. Guarded / zero-cost for crime game. Line 557 `if (agent.state.attributes)` — the crime game declares no attributes, so the property is absent/undefined and the loop body never executes. Correct.

5. attributes is a plain object, not a Map. attributes.ts:67 types it `Record<string, ScalarAttribute>`, so `for...in` enumerates string keys (and would walk the prototype chain in general), and `decayAttribute` (attributes.ts:56-64) is the per-modifier inner loop. The suggested fix `for (const attr of Object.values(agent.state.attributes)) decayAttribute(attr, 5)` is behaviorally equivalent and avoids the prototype-chain idiom.

Caveats on severity (this is genuinely minor, as the finding itself states): the object is created via object literals (createAttribute / save-load), so no enumerable prototype pollution exists in practice, and the loop is fully skipped for the crime game — there is no measurable perf regression today. The finding is real as a naming/consistency wart plus a latent micro-perf idiom on the hot path for future attribute-using modules, which is exactly the (minor) bar the finding claims. Confirmed on its own terms.

reviews.title: attr CG op equality not expressible via the typed comparator
reviews.issue: The attr op switch uses `default: v === target` for equality, but RuleCondition.comparator is typed `'>' | '<' | '>=' | '<='` with no '=' member. reviews.suggestedFix: Either add an explicit '==' to the comparator union and case, or update the comment to state equality is the implicit default when comparator is omitted.
